title: Frontend: Auth context, token storage, and protected route wrapper
description: Set up the auth infrastructure: initialize auth state on app load (by refreshing token), create ProtectedRoute component, and create OAuth callback handler page.
acceptanceCriteria: On app load, attempt to refresh token silently (POST /api/auth/refresh)
If refresh succeeds, populate auth store with user + new token
If refresh fails, user stays on public routes (no redirect loop)
ProtectedRoute component: redirects to /login if not authenticated
OAuth callback page at /auth/callback reads ?token= and stores it
Loading state shown during initial auth check

steps.details: Create src/hooks/useInitAuth.ts. On mount: try POST /api/auth/refresh. If success, GET /api/users/me with the new token, then setAuth(user, accessToken). If fail, clearAuth. Set isLoading = false when done. Return { isLoading }.
In App.tsx or root layout, call useInitAuth(). While isLoading is true, show a full-page spinner. This prevents flash of unauthenticated content.
Create src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx. If !authStore.user, return <Navigate to='/login' replace />. Otherwise render <Outlet />.

Create src/pages/AuthCallbackPage.tsx at route /auth/callback. Read ?token= from URL. If present: store as accessToken in authStore. GET /api/users/me with token. Store user. Navigate to /dashboard. If no token: navigate to /login?error=oauth_failed.
Login, reload page — verify still authenticated (token refreshed). Access /dashboard without auth — verify redirect to /login. Complete Google OAuth — verify callback page sets auth and redirects.
